content.subject: Control Systems
content.hook: Can a polynomial with all positive coefficients still be unstable?
content.question: A system has characteristic equation s cubed plus two s squared plus two s plus forty equals zero. How many roots lie in the right half of the s plane?
content.answerLine: The system has two roots in the right half plane.
explanation: All coefficients are positive, so Stodola's necessary condition passes, but sufficiency requires the full Routh array.
Let us construct the array rows starting from s cubed down to the constant row s zero.
Row s cubed has entries one and two. Row s squared takes the remaining coefficients two and forty.
Now compute the first element of row s one by cross multiplying adjacent coefficients over two.
content.funFact: Edward Routh won the 1854 Cambridge Smith's Prize, placing ahead of the famous James Clerk Maxwell.
content.outro: Master the first column sign test for your AE JE exam and subscribe for more practice.

script.narration: All coefficients are positive, so Stodola's necessary condition passes, but sufficiency requires the full Routh array.
Let us construct the array rows starting from s cubed down to the constant row s zero.
Row s cubed has entries one and two. Row s squared takes the remaining coefficients two and forty.
Now compute the first element of row s one by cross multiplying adjacent coefficients over two.
Multiplying two by two gives four, then subtracting forty gives minus thirty-six, divided by two.
This calculation results in minus eighteen for the first element of the s to the one row.
Next, row s zero pulls down the positive forty term directly below our negative entry.
Inspecting the first column gives positive one, positive two, minus eighteen, and finally positive forty.
There are two sign changes, which means exactly two roots lie in the right half plane.
